text:
maya: quick heads-up — ran a perf pass on staging after the kernel-selector flip to fast-kern-v2. host-side preparse/tokenization CPU is ~2.3x for small requests.

jamal: yikes. did you repro on a different instance type or just rtx-pool?

maya: only rtx-pool so far. same commit on gtx-pool looks fine. suspect kernel scheduling/hot path alignment with our mini-ingress.

ken: can you paste the flame graph? small-requests = <128 tokens?

maya: small (<64) mostly. quick snippet from perf top:
```
  preparse_worker  45.3%  kernel_fast_v2::tokenize
  parse_shim       21.1%  proto_unmarshal
  idle             10.2%  ...
```

sofia: @maya did batching heuristics change too? fast-kern-v2 had an adaptive minibatch hint right?

maya: yes, we enabled auto-mini-batch hint by default. suspected that helped GPU kernel throughput but it adds CPU-side work to coalesce streams.

jamal: could be double work: tokenizer doing prefix normalization then preparse doing it again when batcher merges frames.

maya: exactly. traced a path where tokenize() runs, then preparse sees fragment and re-run normalize for safety.

ingress-bot: deploys/staging/fast-kern-v2 update finished — 1733009600 by maya

ken: can we short-circuit normalize when batcher tags a fragment as already-normalized? cheap flag in frame header?

sofia: that would help. but need to ensure no cross-tenant safety issues. Private deployment might still send unnormalized frames.

maya: proposed change: add one-byte header bit "N" on framed requests from tokenizer service. preparse checks N and skips. simple and cheap.

jamal: how about KV-cache interaction? I saw more KV churn in same window. maybe different alignment causes more small prefixes and thus worse cache hit rate.

maya: KV hotset size didn't change, but miss rate up ~7% for short-lived prefixes. hypothesis: batching reorders requests causing different hash distributions and evictions.

ken: can you dump kvcache evict log for a minute? also tell me sequence lengths distribution pre/post.

maya: attaching short table inline:
```
pre: avg_len=34, p95=58, kvmiss=3.1%
post: avg_len=33, p95=59, kvmiss=10.2%
```

sofia: that's sizable. if batcher groups many small requests into one composite prefix, we may get cache key fragmentation. maybe change keying to use request-root hash instead of per-fragment key.

jamal: note: changing key scheme affects cache reuse for streaming tokens (we rely on fragment keys to resume). need compatibility.

maya: short-term mitigations: 1) disable auto-mini-batch hint for <=64 tokens 2) add header bit N to skip redundant normalize 3) increase kvcache shard size by 10% on rtx-pool.

ken: plan sounds pragmatic. prefer 2 + 1 as quick wins. 3 needs capacity ops signoff.

sofia: I'll open a small PR for the header bit; @maya can add a unit test for cross-tenant safety. jamal, can you run a kvcache sim with rekeying ideas?

jamal: yep, will run sim today and drop numbers here.

maya: quick performance checklist I ran:
- end-to-end latency (50th/95th) for small requests: pre = 42/120ms, post = 48/185ms
- host CPU util preparse: pre = 18%, post = 41%
- tokenization tail allocations +4x

ken: can you capture GRPC vs HTTP paths? might be different because of http2 coalescing.

maya: good call — gRPC path shows more smallwrite syscalls (writev), HTTP/1 path had fewer. streaming chunking heuristics interact with http2 windowing; we'll need to tune http2 framing thresholds.

sofia: for rollout: revert kernel-selector if we don't get quick wins within 24h. we can't regress host costs.

maya: agreed. will land header-bit PR in a couple hours and flip auto-mini-batch off for short requests as a canary. will report back with new perf in ~2h.

jamal: I'll post kvcache sim results ASAP.

ken: thanks team. add any logs or flamegraphs to the thread so we have an audit trail. :thumbsup:

maya: will do — dropping flamegraph + perf flame IDs here when upload completes.
